vo: Why is this whale's tail sticking straight out of the ocean?

label: Seconds earlier
vo: Seconds earlier, this humpback lifted its tail... and tipped its head straight down.
Now its whole body hangs below the surface. Only the tail stays up in the air.
Scientists call this tail sailing. And they still aren't completely sure why it happens.

label: Theory 1
vo: Theory one. It's catching the wind, using its tail as a sail.

label: Theory 2
vo: Theory two. It's cooling down. Warm blood in the tail can shed heat into the air.

label: Theory 3
vo: Theory three. It's simply resting... or playing.
Either way, that tail is one of a kind. Its pattern works like a fingerprint, and scientists use it to identify each whale.
So if you ever see a tail standing still in the ocean...
there's a whale the size of a bus hanging right below it.
